introduction: This guide collects explanations of particular words and verses: what Christ meant by "this generation," by the bread, the rock and the keys; how the darkened sun, the return of Elias, the resurrection and the clouds of heaven are to be read; what Daniel's numbers and the figures of the Revelation refer to; how verses of the Qur’an were understood. Around these examples stand statements of method: take both the outward and the inner meaning, and do not interpret at will. Most of the hundred outside quotations here are therefore the verses themselves, in the King James Bible or Pickthall's Qur’an, placed beside the readings given of them; with them stand the Talmud, Origen, Augustine and Maimonides on method, and Luke, Paul, Hume, Blake and Humpty Dumpty where a reading can be questioned.
questions: Choose one verse and compare it, in its own words, with the explanation given. What does the explanation make clear, and is anything in the verse left over?
"Blessed are they who have taken both the outward and the inner meanings." How does that rule apply to the darkened sun, or to the bread and the body?
The resurrection of Christ is read here as spiritual. How would you answer from these readings the verses in Luke and Paul that seem to say otherwise?
John the Baptist said he was not Elias, and Jesus said he was. What does that pair of verses teach about "return"?
Several passages read dates in Daniel as pointing to the nineteenth century. Newton thought such prophecies were meant to be understood after the event. What follows for how they should be used?
Interpretation "is not as people imagine." What distinguishes a reading from Humpty Dumpty's use of words?

outside.why: The second letter of Peter says that no prophecy of scripture is of private interpretation.
Humpty Dumpty says that a word means just what he chooses it to mean. What makes an interpretation more than that?
Nehemiah tells how the law was read aloud to a later generation, and the Levites gave the sense so that the people understood.
Jesus likens the kingdom to the least of seeds, which becomes a tree.
This is the saying of Jesus that the talk explains, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
This is the verse of the commandments about the third and fourth generation.
Ezekiel says flatly that the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. How do interpreters deal with scriptures that seem to speak against each other?
Aristotle held that the greatest thing by far is to have a command of metaphor.
The rabbis held that a verse never loses its plain meaning, whatever else it teaches.
Paul says that the letter kills and the spirit gives life. Bahá’u’lláh blesses those who take both the outward and the inner meaning. What is the danger in each one alone?
The Qur’an distinguishes clear verses from allegorical ones, and says that none knows their interpretation save God.
Philip asks a man reading Isaiah: understandest thou what thou readest? and he answers: how can I, unless someone guides me?
Blake says to his opponent: thou readest black where I read white. What follows for a community if every reader is his own interpreter?
Augustine asks why, when two readers each find a true meaning, both should not stand. How is that different from speaking "without seeing"?
Paul gathers the whole law into a single saying: love is the fulfilling of the law.
Jesus tells those who search the scriptures that the scriptures testify of him.
Proverbs says, in two verses side by side: answer not a fool according to his folly; answer a fool according to his folly. What do scriptures teach by putting contraries together?
Deuteronomy says: ye shall not add unto the word, neither shall ye diminish from it.
Plato's Socrates says that a written text cannot answer questions and needs its author to defend it. What is the case for one authorized interpreter?
A psalm prays: open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.
This is the saying of Jesus about the sun darkened, the stars falling and the Son of man coming in the clouds.
The Qur’an opens a chapter with the same sign: when the sun is overthrown.
Origen argued that some things in scripture cannot be literal and point the reader to another sense.
Maimonides read the prophets' pictures of the messianic age as figures, and expected the world to keep its course.
The book of Joshua says that the sun stood still in the midst of heaven.
Hume would ask of any report of such a sign whether its falsehood would be more miraculous than the event. Does symbolic reading answer him, or leave his question standing?
Jesus told Pilate that his kingdom was not of this world, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
Two disciples on the road said: we trusted that it had been he who should have redeemed Israel. What happens to an expectation when it is fulfilled in a way no one expected?
This is the prophecy of Isaiah that the talk discusses, of the wolf dwelling with the lamb.
This is the verse of Isaiah about the rod out of the stem of Jesse.
This is the passage of Ezekiel that the letter quotes, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
This is the verse asked about, in which Abraham says: show me how thou givest life to the dead.
Jesus said that Elias had come already and they knew him not.
This is the verse in which John the Baptist says that he is not Elias.
This is the verse in which Jesus says that John is Elias who was to come.
Ezekiel was shown a valley of dry bones and asked: can these bones live?
John records the objection of his hearers: is not this the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how then does he say, I came down from heaven?
This is the verse quoted: no man has ascended to heaven but he that came down from heaven, the Son of man which is in heaven.
Luke has the risen Jesus say: handle me and see, for a spirit has not flesh and bones as ye see me have. How does a spiritual reading of the resurrection deal with this verse?
Paul says that if Christ be not risen, preaching is vain and faith is vain. What did he take the resurrection to be?

This is the passage about the fish and the honeycomb, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.

John tells of Mary saying, "They have no wine," and the answer: mine hour is not yet come.
The Qur’an speaks of the righteous given to drink of a pure wine, sealed.
Jesus promises another Comforter, and speaks of the Spirit as "he.", set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
This is the account of Pentecost, when each heard the apostles in his own language.
Paul says that he would sooner speak five words that are understood than ten thousand in an unknown tongue.
This is the opening of John's Gospel, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
Proverbs speaks of Wisdom as present with God before the world was made.
Jesus asked his disciples: whom say ye that I am?, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
The council of Nicaea answered the question in one way: God of God, Light of Light, of one substance with the Father. What are the other answers named here, and can they stand together?
This is the saying to Peter about the rock, set here in its own words so that it can be read beside the explanation.
John records a like saying: whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted.

The Qur’an says elsewhere that if all the trees were pens, the words of God would not be exhausted.

A psalm says that the world is established and cannot be moved, and it was quoted against Copernicus. What should a reader learn from that episode about scripture and astronomy?
